raw: 415 blood packages   ·   242 Active   ·   generated from packages/blood/ + packages/common/
Blood packages are categorised three separate ways at once, plus a free-text field, and nothing in the
database says which one wins. Before they move to the new catalog schema that has to become one clean
tree. This workbook puts the systems side by side so people who know the business can decide.
READ THIS WITH THE CUSTOM WORKBOOK — the three category tables are SHARED
website_categories, frontend_webpackagecategory and products_packages_products hold custom packages AND
blood packages in the same rows. The usage counts on tabs 1-3 here count BLOOD packages only.
A category showing 0 here may be carrying custom packages — check Custom Package Master Cleanup before
marking anything 'drop'. Decisions taken in either workbook apply to both.
THE THREE TABS — what each one actually is
TAB 1 · Collections            table: website_categories                    71 rows, 3 used by blood
A curated group with its own URL, which can hold packages AND supplements AND coach consultations
in the same group. The only place today where the product families already sit together.
Its category_type column says whether a row holds other groups (MULTI_GROUP) or holds products
BLOOD BARELY USES THIS. Only 8 of 236 blood CMS records are attached to a collection, against much
heavier use by custom packages. Deliberate, or never backfilled? That is question one.
TAB 2 · Package categories     table: frontend_webpackagecategory           143 rows, 25 used by blood
Packages only, one level below a collection. This is the category a package is actually filed under
on the website, and it is reached from the package's CMS record — not from the package itself.
This is the primary filing system for blood: 234 of 236 CMS records carry one.
Read by: CMSPackageRepository, i.e. the website listing and PDP.
TAB 3 · Order path             table: products_packages_products            116 rows, 29 used by blood
NOT customer-facing. This is the classification the cart, order and test-result code reads, and it is
never rendered as a menu — which is why it contains rows like 'Custom Order (Hidden Purpose)'.
Read by: CartServiceImpl, OrderUtils, TestResultServices — the money path.
Plus internal_category, a free-text field on both the package and the CMS row. Not a foreign key,
sparse, but where present often the cleanest signal of the three.
· navigation_menus + navigation_menu_sub_categories drive the home page menu. Not dumped.
· app_package_ranking orders the app listings (367 Blood_Package rows). Dumped but not yet a tab —
it is ordering, not taxonomy, and it belongs in whichever workbook settles the category tree.
· Biomarker composition (tests_subscriptionpackages_tests, 15,023 rows). Out of scope here.
SUB-DEPARTMENT AND CATEGORY ARE TWO DIFFERENT QUESTIONS — both are asked here
DEPARTMENT / SUB-DEPARTMENT     catalog_master.sub_department_id    EXACTLY ONE. Required.
What kind of thing this IS. Structural, permanent, country-agnostic, carries a stable machine code.
DIAGNOSTICS  →  Blood Tests · Functional Tests     (to be defined)
ONE package = ONE sub-department. If something feels like it needs two, give it the single best
structural home and express the second membership as a CATEGORY. Flag it in Notes — if that happens
a lot, the schema needs revisiting, and we would rather learn it here than after it ships.
CATEGORY         catalog_categories                    MANY per package. Optional.
Where it is BROWSABLE. Per country, per channel, freely re-arranged, many-to-many.
Rule of thumb: if moving it would change what the product IS, it is a sub-department.
If it would only change where customers find it, it is a category.
Amber ► columns are yours to fill. Everything else is exported data — please don't edit it, so the
sheet can be regenerated without losing your work.
Work tabs 1 → 2 → 3, not the package list. There are far fewer categories than packages, so a decision
per category settles most packages automatically. Use Package Reconciliation only for what is left over.
Package counts are split Active / Inactive, and the Usage column names the two cases that otherwise look
identical: 'empty' = no blood package points at it, 'dormant' = only inactive ones do. Remember tab 1-3
counts are blood-only — cross-check the custom workbook before dropping.
THINGS TO KNOW BEFORE YOU START
· 'Reachable on website' is derived from the website CMS record only. Whether the mobile app has its own
listing path has NOT been confirmed, so a package marked unreachable may still be live in the app.
· Variants barely exist for blood. frontend_bloodpackagevariants has 7 rows; the custom equivalent has
356. So 'unreachable' here is much closer to literally true than it is in the custom workbook.
· Most unreachable packages are hidden ON PURPOSE — B2B and partner packages (the DEWA and Allianz
sets). Those are labelled separately from genuinely lost ones.
· Two kinds of duplicate, needing different answers. 'Same name, other country' is a country pair and
merges in the new schema. '⚠ Duplicate' is same name or slug within ONE country — one of them is junk,
and seo_meta has a UNIQUE constraint on (country, language, slug), so they cannot all migrate.
· 'Dietitian Consultations' appears 13 times, all in country 1 (ids 114-127). That is not a country
pair. Look at it before writing any merge rule — it may be per-dietitian, i.e. not a category at all.
· Not every row is a category. Several are campaigns or partner buckets — 'Under 99 AED', 'Yellow Friday',
